newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* On Thurday, the Dow Jones closed down 58.11 points, or 0.83 percent, at 6,925.07 points as the market remained unnerved a day after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned that stock prices might be too high and hinted that the central bank may raise interest rates.

* Co-winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, Jose Ramos-Horta of East Timor, urged a Massachusetts legislative committee on Thursday to adopt a measure that would effectively ban companies that do business in Indonesia from doing business with the Commonwealth.

* On Thursday, the Jakarta Composite Index was off 2.69 points, or 0.38 percent, to close at 709.92 points on selling pressure in several blue chips after briefly touching a record high of 717.47 in the morning session, brokers said.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,395.30/96.30 at 0210 GMT, compared with the opening of 2,395.00/96.00
* Cigarette maker Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna after Thursday's annnouncement it posted a net profit of 394 billion rupiah in 1996, compared with its target of 423 billion rupiah.
* Tin miner Tambang Timah following company announcement on Thursday it was planning to buy five mining companies.
* Conglomerate Bimantara Citra on news its South Korean partner Hyundai Motor Co had agreed on a $400 million joint venture with Bimantara to make sedans in Indonesia.
* Garment maker and branded fashion licence holder Great River International on a news report it purchased 15 percent stake in Cluett International Inc. of the United States for 10 billion rupiah.
* Hotel Sahid Jaya on market talk of a possible rights issue.
* Coffee, rubber and tropica trading firm Prasidha Aneka Niaga on analysts expectation that its 1997 would be higher on strong coffee prices.
* Timber firm Barito Pacific on market speculation that business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan was expected to acquire a stake in the company through his paper producer PT Kiani Kertas.

* Holding company Bakrie & Brothers on market talk that it would set up a consortium with some Indonesian businessmen and Bank Bumiputera Bhd of Malaysia to help the troubled private-owned Bank Pacific.
* Budi Acid Jaya on reports that its 1996 profits would be higher than analysts' forecasts.
